t: That section 4 of the Act of August 9, 1946 (Public Law 711, Seventy-ninth Congress), is amended by deleting therefrom the date “January 3, 1947” and inserting in lieu thereof the date “January 3, 1948”.

fable.w: This section only amends a prior Act by replacing one date with another, extending a deadline by a year. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by deleting therefrom the date “January 3, 1947” and inserting in lieu thereof the date “January 3, 1948”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple amendment to a previous statute, changing a specific date. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative housekeeping measure.
qwen_block.s: That section 4 of the Act of August 9, 1946 (Public Law 711, Seventy-ninth Congress), is amended by deleting therefrom the date “January 3, 1947” and inserting in lieu thereof the date “January 3, 1948”.

opus.w: This section only changes a date in an earlier Act. It names no outside party and sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period or right to sue. It's tempting to guess that the underlying 1946 law set up a commission, but nothing in this section's text shows any outside participation in a federal decision.
opus.s: is amended by deleting therefrom the date “January 3, 1947” and inserting in lieu thereof the date “January 3, 1948”
opus.b:
The section only swaps one date for another in an earlier law, so it doesn't require participation.

1. **The tempting reading:** Public Law 711 of the 79th Congress could have set up a commission or a consultation process. If so, pushing its deadline from 1947 to 1948 might seem to extend outside participation.
2. **Why that fails:** The text of this section names no commission, no hearing, no consultation and no outside party. Only the dates appear. I can't tell what the 1946 law did from this text, and a bare amendment to a date doesn't on its face bring anyone outside the federal government into a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply amends a date in a previous statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. There is no mention of public hearings, advisory committees, state consultation, or comment periods.
qwen_chat.s: That section 4 of the Act of August 9, 1946 (Public Law 711, Seventy-ninth Congress), is amended by deleting therefrom the date “January 3, 1947” and inserting in lieu thereof the date “January 3, 1948”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a deadline could affect public participation if the deadline was for a comment period. However, the text itself does not mention any public process, comment period, or hearing; it merely amends a date in a previous act. Without explicit reference to an outside party's involvement in a decision, this is just a procedural amendment.
